root_cause.text: The boundary check in `decode_choice()` uses an uninitialized `len` variable (value 0) instead of checking for the 2 bytes that `get_len()` may read, allowing an out-of-bounds read when the bitstream is exactly consumed.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `nf_h323_error_boundary(bs, len, 0)` to `nf_h323_error_boundary(bs, 2, 0)` at line 799. The CVE description explains that when `bs->cur == bs->end`, the check `nf_h323_error_boundary(bs, 0, 0)` evaluates to `(bs->cur + 0 > bs->end)` which is false, allowing the subsequent `get_len()` call to dereference `*bs->cur++` and read 1-2 bytes past the buffer end. The fix matches the pattern used at all other `get_len()` call sites in the file, which check for 2 bytes of available data before calling `get_len()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix boundary validation in H.323 choice decoding by checking for a minimum of 2 bytes instead of using an uninitialized or incorrect length variable.
intent_record.what: Changed the second argument to nf_h323_error_boundary() from variable 'len' to literal constant '2' on line 799.
intent_record.how: This modifies the boundary check validation logic to use a fixed minimum length of 2 bytes instead of the variable length value. This affects how the function validates whether sufficient bytes are available in the bitstream before proceeding with decoding, potentially changing which error conditions are detected.

candidates.rationale: This boundary check at line 799 uses the uninitialized `len` variable (which has value 0 from a previous iteration or initialization) before `len` is assigned the actual value from `get_len(bs)` at line 801. This allows an out-of-bounds read when the bitstream is exactly consumed, as the check should validate that at least 2 bytes are available for `get_len()` to read, not check against the uninitialized/stale `len` value.

vuln_statements.explanation: This boundary check at line 799 uses the uninitialized or stale `len` variable (value 0) to validate bitstream bounds before `len` is assigned the actual value from `get_len(bs)` at line 801. The check should validate that at least 2 bytes are available for the subsequent `get_len()` call to safely read, but instead it checks against an incorrect/uninitialized `len` value, allowing an out-of-bounds read when the bitstream is exactly consumed.

Author: Eric Sesterhenn <eric.sesterhenn@x41-dsec.de>

    netfilter: nf_ct_h323: Extend nf_h323_error_boundary to work on bits as well
    
    This patch fixes several out of bounds memory reads by extending
    the nf_h323_error_boundary() function to work on bits as well
    an check the affected parts.
    
    Signed-off-by: Eric Sesterhenn <eric.sesterhenn@x41-dsec.de>
    Signed-off-by: Pablo Neira Ayu
bic_trace_step.reason: This commit FIXES the vulnerability rather than introducing it. The root cause describes an uninitialized `len` variable (value 0) being used in boundary checks instead of checking for the 2 bytes that `get_len()` may read. In this commit, the `nf_h323_error_boundary()` function is extended to accept a `bits` parameter, and crucially, boundary checks are added BEFORE calls to `get_len()` and `get_bits()` that could read from the bitstream. For example, at line 337-338 in decode_int(): `if (nf_h323_error_boundary(bs, 0, 2)) return H323_ERROR_BOUND;` is added before `len = get_bits(bs, 2) + 1;`. Similarly, at lines 809-811 in decode_choice(): `if (nf_h323_error_boundary(bs, 2, 0)) return H323_ERROR_BOUND;` is added before `len = get_len(bs);`. These checks ensure the bitstream has sufficient data before attempting to read, preventing the out-of-bounds read vulnerability. The vulnerable construct (using uninitialized len in boundary checks) is not present in this code - instead, proper boundary checks are performed before reading operations.
